one_liner: Goes in the too-hard pile: its industry is changing too fast to predict. No verdict on price.

profile.what: Alphabet owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Google Cloud and Gemini AI, plus long-term bets including Waymo self-driving cars.
profile.money: Advertising on Search and YouTube is about three-quarters of revenue: businesses pay when users click or view ads. Google Cloud sells computing and AI services and is now profitable. Subscriptions (YouTube Premium, Google One) and Pixel devices add the rest.
profile.valued: Alphabet is valued on P/E and free cash flow. It has traded at a discount to other large tech companies because of fears that AI chatbots replace search and antitrust remedies; the multiple rises with evidence that Gemini and Cloud strengthen the business.

summary.sentence: The dominant search and video advertising business, spending heavily to defend it in the AI era.
strengths: Trailing P/E under 15 is cheap for this quality.
Cloud and Gemini are real growth engines.
Fortress balance sheet with large net cash.
risks: Search faces its first serious technology threat in two decades.
TTM net income is inflated by non-operating gains; operating margin is a more honest 33%.
AI capex has cut TTM free cash flow to under $20B.

meaning.what_it_does: Owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Google Cloud and the Waymo and DeepMind bets.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: Mostly advertising on Search and YouTube, plus Google Cloud and subscriptions.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: Billions of daily users and unmatched data keep advertisers coming; Cloud and Gemini AI add new revenue streams.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: AI chat assistants could replace the search box, cutting the ad clicks that fund everything; antitrust remedies could weaken default search deals.

moat.summary: Search still dominates and YouTube has no real peer. The moat is wide today, but its durability is being tested by AI.

industry.summary: Generative AI is changing how people find information. Search now has to out-innovate rivals to keep its position: the technology-war pattern the framework avoids.

management.summary: Strong engineering and a cleaner capital-return programme (buybacks plus a new dividend), but heavy spending on long-shot bets and AI capex.

financial_health.ratio_gaps: Not available from the data source, so not shown: a ten-year record, inventory and receivables turnover, the quick ratio, goodwill and tangible book value, and maintenance capex split from growth capex. Owner earnings therefore deduct all capex, which is conservative.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow, capex held at depreciation: $102.9B a year: operating cash flow less depreciation and stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). Capex is running at 5.6x depreciation, so most of it is expansion, not upkeep. (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 7–13% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 33%; cost of capital 10.5%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
